title: Predominance in damages classes
summary: Predominance asks whether common questions are sufficiently important and cohesive relative to individual questions for the proposed Rule 23(b)(3) treatment. It is more demanding than the presence of one shared question.
notes: Predominance is not a simple numerical count of shared and individual questions. Settlement removes trial-manageability concerns, but does not erase this separate requirement.

sections.Meaning: Predominance asks whether common questions are sufficiently important and cohesive relative to individual questions for the proposed Rule 23(b)(3) treatment. It is more demanding than the presence of one shared question.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the elements requiring proof, what can be established commonly, and which issues require individual adjudication. Consider variation in causation, injury, defenses, and governing law. Amchem shows why a common interest in settlement does not replace this assessment.
